Medical Robots

By: Mart-Marie Faure | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Would you like to have a robot cut into your bones or perform heart surgery, it's not just science fiction, medical robots are making waves right here in South African operating theatres.

Unique Selling Point:
Soon autonomous robots could be a regular member of any hospital's medical staff, performing duties from taking a patient's pulse and scanning vital signs, to reading case notes and even performing surgery. Some might say thats just science fiction but doctor controlled-robots already have a massive presence in the medical field, and demand for the less invasive, more patient tailored, doctor controlled procedures are growing. Now, in a first in Africa , two South African doctors are performing robotic-assisted total knee replacements and robotic coronary angioplaties.

Summary:
Robotic surgery first became popular in the 1980s. The first surgery was performed in 1985 when a robot was used to improve precision in neurosurgical biopsies and the da Vinci system was used for prostate surgery. Surgery is the most commonly used robotic application in healthcare. Sadly South Africa has been lagging behind, that is until recently. In December last year Dr Faizel Lorgat at the Christiaan Barnard Memorial hospital in Cape Town, an interventional cardiologist succesfully completed the firsts robotic coronary angioplasties in Africa. In Johannesburg, Dr Chris McCready, performed the first state-of-the-art robotic knee replacement operation. This technology could signal a new era in personalised joint replacement.


Further information:
An estimated 8000 to 10 000 knee replacements are performed in SA. This new technology could signal a new era in personalised joint replacement. The advanced system is already well established in Europe, the US and the UK.The system was used in over 250 000procedures internationally last year. One of the major advances of the robotic-assisted surgical system is that, prior to surgery, it draws data from a CT scan of the patient's knee to develop a three-dimensional pre-operative plan that is unique to each individual.The technology determines the dimension for the surgical cuts to the bone surfaces so that the best sized implanted joint components can be selected for each patient. During the operation, the robotic arm system provides detailed visual, auditory and tactile feedback to the surgeon.
Dr Faizel lorgat is an experienced medical robotics practitioner. He was one of the first robotic operators worldwide in the vascular sector. Six interventions have successfully been completed.

Press Release:


Robotic Surgery
How would you feel having a robot on your surgical team in the operating theatre? Steadily on the rise in Europe and America, robot-assisted surgery is now available in South Africa. We track the benefits and risks involved when patients go under the knife with robot assistants performing delicate and complex procedures.
Producer: Mart-Marie Faure | Presenter: Claire Mawisa


Script:


Medical Robots

Promo 1
State of the art medical robots are taking their place in South African operating theatres, assisting in heart procedures and placing prostheses in knees and hips with precision.
Promo 2
Robots cutting into bone or delivering stents to your heart, state of the art surgeries are being performed for the first time, right here in South
African operating theatres.
Promo 3
In a first for Africa, two South African surgeons are performing groundbreaking cardiovascular procedures and joint replacement surgeries with the use of state of the art robotic technology.
EVA




06:24 My sister passed away. I got a letter from my sister’s physician to say they were disconnecting her. And the same day I felt this pain.
07:22 Like a vibration in my left shoulder.

08:44 I listened to my body and my mother had heart attacks s And so I thought ,well it runs in the family.



ClaireV/O















With a family history of heart disease, Eva Weincove feared the worst. She approached cardiologist Dr Faizel Lorgat. The prognosis; that she needed intervention and quickly.


Claire V/O
The use of a brand new cardiovascular robotic system for the procedure was suggested. Eva agreed , and she became the first patient in Africa to undergo a robotic coronary angioplasty.
Eva








01:20 It was a very big artery into my heart, an important one and if I hadn't gone in I would have had a heart attack.
He said I could come back and he would try the robotic way.

Claire V/O
Last year more than a million robotic medical procedures were performed worldwide. South Africa has been lagging behind, that is until recently when two state of the art medical robots, one geared for heart procedures, the other for total joint replacements, arrived on our shores.
Claire link
South African doctors have a long tradition of being on the cutting edge of medicine, just like Dr Chris Barnard who performed a groundbreaking heart transplant surgery in 1967. Recently history was made when a leading cardiologist performed the first successful robotic -assisted angioplasty in Africa, right here in Cape Town.
Dr Faizal Lorgat



09:24 The advantage of using robotic assistance is that we now have a device which is able to enhance the precision of the human hand. 02:28 It is able to control guide wires and also deliver balloons and stents.
Claire V/O
Dr Lorgat is a recognized interventional cardiologist at the Chris Barnard Memorial Hospital, and an experienced medical robotics practitiioner…
Dr Faizel Lorgat,






Claire V/O








Claire/Eva







Claire V/O


Lorgat must explain
____________________________________________________
____________________________________________________________
Through the access point the guide wires are deployed to deliver the balloon with precision, enabling it to open blocked arteries.

____________________________________________________
You were the first to have this robotic assisted surgery, weren't you afraid.

He wasn't going to kill me, why would he. I didn't do anything to harm him . Why should he. laugh I didn’t do anything to him. I’ve done nothing to harm him. Laugh


____________________________________________________




In Johannesburg, robot technology has also been making waves.
Claire Link
Orthopeadic surgeon Dr Chris Mc Cready has ushered in a new era in joint replacements by using state of the art robotics to perform total knee replacement surgeries.
Dr Chris Mc Cready




Claire V/O

In the past--------X ray


_________________________________________________
The robot draws data from a CT scan of the patient’s knee to develop a 3 dimensional plan that is unique to each patient.

John Thompson



06:01 Some 15 years ago I had a bad fall trying to do.. To jump over a stream and missed and landed on my knee on a rock and broke the patella, got fixed up, but it was never the same. This is beginning to to affect my mobility, , my getting around. There was more pain.
Dr Mc Cready
Mc Cready
In the past……………..
Claire V/O





Claire V/O



Claire V/O
During the operation , the robotic arm system provides detailed visual, auditory and tactile feedback to the surgeon,


The robotic arm locks into position where the cut should be made. If the blade drifts out of position , the robot will cut the power to the saw blade.



What remains , is for the glue to be mixed and the prosthesis put in place with robotic precision.





Everything went well



Claire Link
John has just been wheeled out of theatre and from what we saw on the screens, it was a success.


Claire Question





Claire Question


Dr McCready





Dr Lorgat




Claire V/O



Neil Kirby








Claire V/O











Anna-Marie de Wet









Claire V/O










Claire Question




Dr Mc Cready




Dr Lorgat













































Will these medical robots be part of the medical team team going forward?
Well we called ours Bob,so at least we have given him a name and a personality.

06:14: For somebody sitting on the couch there thinking oh my gosh what if something goes wrong.

06:37 We can simply revert back to the standard original way of doing joint replacement. At the moment we have had no failures and I think hardly any failures have been reported in the world

This is the first generation, the next generation which is on our doorstep with both artificial and machine learning. Ultimately these machines will be cleverer than us.
_________________________________________________
So what happens when Bob becomes autonomous and starts to operate independently from us humans? What happens if things go wrong , who would be to blame?

_________________________________________________
03:14There are two sets of liabilities that potentially arise .
A liability that would arise from medical negligence if one can show that there was a deficiency in the the process in either the ability of the robot to assess and address what was then confronted with at the time. I would think then that a patient would have recourse against the manufacturer of the robot insofar that the manufacturer was also responsible for the import of any software.
________________________________________________

Neil Kirby heads Healthcare and Life Sciences at Werkman’s Attorneys.

_________________________________________________

Under the Consumer Act where a patient would have the choice of instituting proceedings against the entire supply chain of the robot it would include the doctor.




13:56 The robotic surgery has changed my life in a positive way. I am able to walk better because the knee was so damaged. 10:17 Sleeping was a problem because of the pain.I was sleeping really badly at night because the pain was something else. I started going to physio, trying to strengthen, but the extent of the damage in the knee was so bad. I actually said its so bad Im at the point where , just cut the knee off.

_________________________________________________
The agonising pain from her damaged knee had a detrimental effect on Anne-Marie de Wet’s mental well being and life style. She was the first patient in South Africa to undergo a total knee replacement with the new technology.

________________________________________________
09:32 The technology they brought out with this, I think it is brilliant. Because in the old days they had to chisel fit, chisel fit, where now it’s precision.
_________________________________________________
02:45: So what are the advantages of using this robot in surgeries?

The better the components are put in and the better they are aligned, then potentially you are going to have less postoperative pain. You are going to recover and rehabilitate quicker , You will most likely regain more function if you are having better alignment of your components.


09:08: We are human cardiologists, we get tired and people who get tired make mistakes. We have never lost a patient during robotic procedure and that is the testimony of the efficiency of these systems.






I can foresee in a decade or even sooner that we realise that these robot systems will be able to perform the procedures independently of us humans.
